title: Red-first has one vocabulary and a safe mechanism, and doctor's plugin rows say what is true
desiredOutcome: executor, reviewer and schema share one redFirst vocabulary checked by a lint; a sanctioned red-first helper proves red in a throwaway tree without touching the shared one, and a compile or collection failure is not a proved red; and doctor's running-plugin and plugin-files rows grade on evidence a new session or a marketplace install can actually clear

tasks.title: One redFirst vocabulary, a sanctioned red-first helper, and a compile failure is not a proved red
tasks.description: Reproduced at HEAD: executor and schema say proved|could-not-prove|not-attempted; the reviewer says proved|not-proved|could-not-prove|not-applicable, misquotes the executor (reviewer.md:67) and has no word for regression mode. The schema enum is the one source; the reviewer echoes the executor's word when its basis holds; not-attempted replaces not-applicable; not-proved stays as a DECLARED reviewer-only grade; a _refs lint checks reviewer words are within schema plus declared reviewer-only. The executor brief sends executors to overwrite shared files to prove red (undo the fix in the shared tree, git show HEAD:f > f), which the host refused beside a sibling's uncommitted work: add stamp-verification.py red --task <id> -- <cmd> that builds a throwaway tree (git worktree add --detach or a git archive scratch) with HEAD's version of the task's implementation files and the working tree's test files, runs the command there, and records the red, never touching the shared tree; the briefs point at it. proved requires at least one test collected and an assertion failure; a compile or collection error is could-not-prove unless the task introduces the symbol.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test__refs.py: repro that FAILS on current code - the reviewer brief grades redFirst with not-proved/not-applicable, which the schema enum rejects, and no lint notices

outcome.technical: _refs.red_first_vocabulary_drift over the schema enum; stamp-verification.py red in a throwaway detached worktree; collection errors are could-not-prove unless --introduces.
outcome.descriptive: Red-first has one vocabulary across executor, reviewer and schema, and can be proved without touching the shared tree.

tasks.title: Doctor's running-plugin and plugin-files rows grade on evidence a new session or a marketplace install can actually clear
tasks.description: Reproduced at HEAD (and live on this repo): running_plugin_verdict counts any stamp that is not this copy as drift and never reads the mtime it records, so a dead session's stamp holds the row yellow and 'start a new session' cannot clear it - grade on the newest stamp per copy with its age, report an older copy that a newer one has stamped since as history (named, aged), and offer a prune. plugin_integrity assumes a marketplace install is a clone; the cache is not (installed_plugins.json records installPath and gitCommitSha, and the marketplace clone holds that commit) - compare the cache tree with git archive of that SHA from the marketplace clone, unverifiable only when either is missing (these are undocumented Claude Code files; say so as /audit:version does).

add: plugins/audit/tests/test__doctor_trail.py: repro that FAILS on current code - one six-day-old stamp from a dead session naming an older plugin holds the running-plugin row at WARNING while every newer stamp names the running copy

outcome.technical: split_history grades the newest stamp per copy; cache_integrity compares the cache with git archive of the recorded commit; readers in _claude_home.
outcome.descriptive: Doctor stops warning about a dead session's old plugin stamp and verifies a marketplace install instead of calling it unverifiable.
